blocks.prompt: 7 (a) Convert each of the following equation into (i) Slope-intercept form (ii) Two-point form (iii) Intercept form (iv) Point-slope form (v) Normal form (vi) Symmetric form: \(2x + 3y - 6 = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Yahan ek hi line ko chhe tareeqon se likhna hai. Line wohi rehti hai, sirf us ka 'libaas' badalta hai.
Har form line ki koi khaas baat dikhati hai: slope, do points, intercepts, ek point aur slope, origin se perpendicular faasla, ya inclination.
Is liye pehle slope aur dono intercepts nikal lete hain; baqi sab forms inhi se ban jati hain.
Kitab ne is sawal ke jawab nahi diye, is liye hum har form ko aakhir mein wapas khol kar tasdeeq karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(2x + 3y - 6 = 0\).
Maloom karna: chhe standard forms (i)-(vi).
Tareeqa: bilkul Example 6 ki tarah. Slope ke liye \(y\) ko akela karenge; two-point aur point-slope form ke liye do intercept points \((x\text{-intercept}, 0)\) aur \((0, y\text{-intercept})\) lenge; normal form ke liye \(\pm\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) se divide; symmetric form ke liye \(\tan\theta = m\) se \(\sin\theta\), \(\cos\theta\).

(i) Slope-intercept form
\[3y = -2x + 6\]
\[y = -\dfrac{2}{3}x + 2\]
Kyun: \(y\) ko akela kiya, to \(y = mx + c\) ki shakal ban gayi; slope \(m = -\frac{2}{3}\) aur \(y\)-intercept \(c = 2\). Yeh form slope foran bata deti hai.
Dhyan dein: \(c\) yahan \(y\)-intercept hai, line ki equation wala constant nahi; dono ko alag samjhein.

Line par do points
\(y = 0\) rakhein to \(x = 3\); \(x = 0\) rakhein to \(y = 2\). Points \((3, 0)\) aur \((0, 2)\).
Kyun: axes wale points sab se aasani se milte hain, kyunke ek coordinate zero hota hai (kitab bhi yahi leti hai).

(ii) Two-point form
\[\dfrac{y - 0}{2 - 0} = \dfrac{x - 3}{0 - 3}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{y - y_1}{y_2 - y_1} = \frac{x - x_1}{x_2 - x_1}\) mein \((x_1, y_1) = (3, 0)\) aur \((x_2, y_2) = (0, 2)\) rakhe. Koi aur do points bhi le sakte the; jawab ki shakal badlegi, line wohi rahegi.

(iii) Intercept form
\[2x + 3y = 6\]
\[\dfrac{2x}{6} + \dfrac{3y}{6} = 1\]
\[\dfrac{x}{3} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 1\]
Kyun: constant ko right side le gaye aur usi se divide kiya taake right side 1 ban jaye; ab neeche intercepts nazar aate hain: \(a = 3\), \(b = 2\).
Intercept form ka faida: line ka graph foran ban jata hai, bas dono axes par intercepts mark kar ke jor do.

(iv) Point-slope form
\[y - 0 = -\dfrac{2}{3}(x - 3)\]
Kyun: \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) mein point \((3, 0)\) aur \(m = -\frac{2}{3}\) rakhe.
Point-slope form asal mein slope ki definition hai: kisi bhi point \((x, y)\) aur \((x_1, y_1)\) ke darmiyan slope \(m\) hi rehti hai.

(v) Normal form
\[\sqrt{2^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{13}\]
\[\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{13}}x + \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{13}}y = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{13}}\]
Kyun: line ko \(ax + by = -c\) likh kar \(+\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) se divide karte hain taake right side \(p\) positive rahe (\(p\) origin se line ka faasla hai, faasla negative nahi hota). Yahan right side pehle hi positive hai, is liye \(+\) sign. Ab \(x\cos\alpha + y\sin\alpha = p\) jahan \(\cos\alpha = \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}, \sin\alpha = \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}, p = \frac{6}{\sqrt{13}}\) (\(\alpha \approx 56.31^\circ\)).
Yaad rakhein: \(\cos\alpha\) aur \(\sin\alpha\) ke squares ka jama 1 hona chahiye; yeh ek foran wali tasdeeq hai ke humne sahi number se divide kiya.

(vi) Symmetric form
\[\tan\theta = -\dfrac{2}{3}\]
\[\sin\theta = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\]
\[\cos\theta = -\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\]
\[\dfrac{x - 3}{-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}} = \dfrac{y - 0}{\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}} = r\]
Kyun: \(\theta\) line ka inclination (x-axis se jhukao) hai, \(0^\circ \le \theta < 180^\circ\), is liye \(\sin\theta\) kabhi negative nahi. \(\tan\theta\) negative hai, to \(\theta\) obtuse (90 se bara) hai aur \(\cos\theta\) negative. Phir \(\frac{x - x_1}{\cos\theta} = \frac{y - y_1}{\sin\theta} = r\) mein point \((3, 0)\) rakha.
Dhyan dein: \(\sin\theta\) aur \(\cos\theta\) ke signs \(\tan\theta\) ke sign se milne chahiyein; \(\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\) dobara slope de to sahi hai.
Symmetric form mein \(r\) line par us point se faasla hai jo humne liya; \(r\) badlo to line ke saare points mil jate hain.

Tasdeeq:
Symmetric form ko cross-multiply karein:
\[\tfrac{2}{\sqrt{13}}(x - 3) = -\tfrac{3}{\sqrt{13}}y\]
\[2x + 3y - 6 = 0\]
jo bilkul di hui equation hai. Har form ko isi tarah wapas khol kar check kar sakte hain. (Kitab ne is sawal ke jawab nahi diye; agar aap ne koi aur points liye hon to aap ki form bhi sahi hai, bas khol kar wohi line aani chahiye.)
